title: The three requisites of a valid inquiry (Sec. 21)
ask: Under Art. VI, Sec. 21, what must every inquiry by either House or its committees satisfy?
items: It must be in aid of legislation (judged by the speech or resolution behind it)
It must follow duly published rules of procedure (published in each Congress, in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation)
The rights of persons appearing in, or affected by, the inquiry must be respected
src: Art. VI, Sec. 21; Bengzon v. Senate Blue Ribbon; Garcillano

title: Who may refuse to appear or answer before an inquiry
ask: Name the ways a person can lawfully avoid testifying before a congressional inquiry in aid of legislation.
items: The President: exempt from the power of inquiry
Justices of the Supreme Court: exempt
Anyone with a valid claim of executive privilege, made by the President or the Executive Secretary by order of the President, for specific information
Military officers barred by the Commander-in-Chief, until a court orders them to appear
A witness facing a specific incriminating question (self-incrimination, invoked question by question)
src: Senate v. Ermita; Gudani v. Senga; Ong v. Senate Tricomm
hook: Two exempt persons, then privilege, the Commander-in-Chief, and one question at a time.

title: Question hour (Sec. 22) versus inquiry (Sec. 21)
ask: Give the differences between the question hour and an inquiry in aid of legislation.
items: Purpose: oversight (Sec. 22) versus legislation (Sec. 21)
Who: heads of departments only versus anyone
Attendance: discretionary, with the President's consent, versus compulsory by subpoena
Way out of Sec. 21: only a valid claim of privilege, or the President's and SC Justices' exemption
Sec. 22 may be in executive session when the President states in writing that security or public interest requires

title: The presidential communications privilege (Neri)
ask: When are presidential communications presumptively privileged?
items: The communication relates to a quintessential and non-delegable presidential power
It was authored, or solicited and received, by the President or a close advisor in operational proximity
No adequate showing of compelling need and unavailability of the information elsewhere overcomes it (against Congress: critical to legislation, not merely pertinent)
hook: Quintessential power, Proximity, No compelling need.

title: How executive privilege must be claimed
ask: What makes a claim of executive privilege procedurally valid?
items: It is claimed by the President, or the Executive Secretary 'by order of the President'
It is express and specific: it states the kind of privilege and the reasons
It covers kinds of information, not categories of persons (a blanket consent requirement is void)

title: When contempt detention must end (Balag)
ask: Until when may a witness be detained under the inherent contempt power of the Senate?
items: Until the committee report is approved or disapproved
Or until the Congress that started the inquiry ends (whichever comes first); recess does not end it
hook: The report or the Congress, whichever ends first.

title: Valid contempt by a committee
ask: What must a committee do before and when citing a witness in contempt?
items: Give the witness a chance to explain, at least when citing for false or evasive testimony
Vote by a majority of all its members, after deliberation (Senate Rules, Sec. 18)
Act under rules duly published in that Congress
Detain only until the inquiry ends; longer punishment needs statutory contempt in court
src: Ong v. Senate (2023); Neri; Garcillano; Balag

title: Remedies against a legislative inquiry
ask: What remedies are, and are not, open to a witness who objects to an inquiry or is detained by Congress?
items: Habeas corpus: the SC, CA and RTC have concurrent jurisdiction; the SC will not take a case already with the CA
Certiorari or prohibition under the expanded jurisdiction, on a showing of grave abuse or unconstitutionality
If the President challenges the inquiry's legislative purpose, the committee must resolve it first; direct resort is premature
Not amparo: only extralegal killings and enforced disappearances
src: Agcaoili v. Fariñas; Senate v. Medialdea
hook: Habeas yes, prohibition with abuse, committee first, amparo no.

title: Sec. 26(2): what a certification of urgency waives
ask: Which requirements of Art. VI, Sec. 26(2) does a presidential certification of urgency dispense with, and which remain?
items: Waived: readings on separate days
Waived: printed copies in final form distributed three days before passage
Remains: three readings
Remains: no amendment on the last reading
Remains: the vote taken immediately, with the yeas and nays entered in the Journal
src: Art. VI, Sec. 26(2); Kida v. Senate; Tolentino
hook: Certification waives the days, not the readings.

title: The item veto
ask: State the rules on the President's item veto.
items: Only in appropriation, revenue or tariff bills; other bills are vetoed whole or not at all
An item is an indivisible sum of money dedicated to a stated purpose
Inappropriate provisions (general legislation unrelated to an appropriation) may be vetoed as items
The President may not veto part of an item, or a provision that is not an item
A veto cannot dictate how a fiscally autonomous body uses its funds, or repeal an existing law
Override: two-thirds of all the Members of each House; a bill not vetoed within 30 days becomes law
src: Art. VI, Sec. 27; Gonzales v. Macaraig; Bengzon v. Drilon
hook: ART bills; whole items or riders; no slicing, no dictating.

title: Things that are not laws
ask: Name measures the Court has held cannot amend or make law.
items: A joint resolution, even if passed like a bill (Ang Nars)
A plan that takes effect because Congress failed to disapprove it (Miller v. Mardo)
A presidential veto used to repeal an existing law (Bengzon v. Drilon)
src: Ang Nars; Miller v. Mardo; Bengzon v. Drilon
hook: Only a bill, passed and signed, is law.

title: Congress and the Supreme Court's jurisdiction
ask: What may Congress not do to the Supreme Court's jurisdiction and rules?
items: Increase the Court's appellate jurisdiction without its advice and concurrence (Art. VI, Sec. 30; Fabian)
Prescribe rules of pleading, practice and procedure, which belong to the Court (Art. VIII, Sec. 5(5); Carpio-Morales)
Deprive the Court of its jurisdiction under Art. VIII, Sec. 5 (Art. VIII, Sec. 2)
src: Fabian v. Desierto; Carpio-Morales v. CA
hook: No A&C, no appeal; the rules are the Court's.
